title: Copyright Office Probes AI's Role in Streaming Fraud
key_facts: The US Copyright Office launched an investigation into music streaming fraud, which Billboard calls one of the music industry's biggest problems.

A Wednesday (7 Oct 2026) notice in the Federal Register says the office is soliciting data and suggestions that may contribute to Congress's understanding of streaming fraud, current efforts to curb it and potential solutions.
The inquiry responds to a letter sent in May by Rep. Scott Fitzgerald (R-Wis.), who asked the office to examine how generative AI can serve as a catalyst for criminals to perpetrate streaming fraud.
The Billboard text read does not say the notice itself names AI.
quote_evidence: The U.S. Copyright Office has launched an investigation into one of the music industry's biggest problems: streaming fraud.
The congressman ... said in this letter that the Copyright Office should specifically examine the ways "generative AI can serve as a catalyst for criminals to perpetrate streaming fraud."
why_it_matters_hint: Musicians, rights holders and listeners may see new policy on fake streams, and the AI question enters through a congressman's letter.
notes: Pool item is Law360 (paywalled; headline frames the inquiry as probing AI's role). Billboard read for its first 3,388 characters. Chosen category LAW (copyright); chunk default POL or LAW.
